skills.name: Interior angle sums

steps.c: one angle of a regular polygon

skills.wrong_turn: Use n − 2 triangles, not n. A pentagon's angles sum to 3 × 180° = 540°, not 900°.
skills.rule: The interior angles of an n-gon sum to (n−2)⋅180°.

skills.name: Exterior angle sum
skills.wrong_turn: Don't mix up the two sums. The exterior angles always total 360°; it's the interior sum, (n − 2)·180°, that grows with n.
skills.rule: The exterior angles of a convex polygon, one at each vertex, sum to 360°.

skills.name: Parallelogram properties
skills.wrong_turn: A parallelogram's diagonals bisect each other but are usually not equal. Only in a rectangle are they the same length.
skills.rule: A parallelogram has opposite sides and opposite angles congruent, consecutive angles supplementary, and diagonals that bisect each other.

skills.name: Proving parallelograms
skills.wrong_turn: One pair of parallel sides isn't enough: that could be a trapezoid. You need both pairs, or one pair parallel and congruent.
skills.rule: Show both pairs of opposite sides congruent, or one pair congruent and parallel, or diagonals that bisect each other.

skills.name: Rectangles, rhombi, squares
skills.wrong_turn: A rectangle's diagonals are equal but not perpendicular. Only when all sides are equal too, in a square, do they cross at right angles.
skills.rule: Rectangle: diagonals congruent. Rhombus: diagonals perpendicular and bisecting the angles. Square: all of these.

skills.name: Trapezoids & kites
skills.wrong_turn: The trapezoid midsegment averages the two bases; it doesn't halve one. Bases 10 and 16 give 13, not 8.
skills.rule: Trapezoid midsegment =(b1+b22). A kite's diagonals are perpendicular.

skills.name: Quadrilateral family tree
skills.wrong_turn: "Sometimes" isn't "never". A rectangle is sometimes a rhombus: exactly when it's a square.
skills.rule: Each shape inherits every property of the shapes above it in the family tree.

skills.name: Regular polygon area
skills.wrong_turn: The apothem goes to the middle of a side, not to a corner. Using the radius instead of the apothem overstates the area.
skills.rule: A=(12)aP, where a is the apothem and P the perimeter.

skills.name: Coordinate proofs
skills.wrong_turn: Use letters, not specific numbers. Checking the rectangle (0, 0), (4, 0), (4, 3), (0, 3) proves nothing about every rectangle.
skills.rule: Place the figure to keep coordinates simple, then use the slope, distance and midpoint formulas.
